exposure: maternal stress during the third trimester of pregnancy (measured by Cohen's Perceived Stress Scale)
outcome: abundance of specific bacterial taxa (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Bacteroides, Enterobacteriaceae) in the infant gut
cohort: Fifty-one women recruited during their third trimester of pregnancy and their neonates, from whom a stool sample was collected at one month of age.
finding: More severe maternal prenatal stress was associated with a greater diversity of microbial species in the neonate's gut microbiome at one month of age, with enrichment of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, and depletion of Bacteroides and Enterobacteriaceae.
